parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.stem:
Nitrogen monoxide, $\text{NO}$, reacts with hydrogen, as shown in reaction 3.

reaction 3 $$2\text{NO} + 2\text{H}_2 \rightarrow \text{N}_2 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$$
parts.text:
The rate equation for reaction 3 is shown.

$$\text{rate} = k[\text{H}_2][\text{NO}]^2$$

Complete Table 4.1.

Table 4.1

|  |  |
| :--- | :--- |
| the order of reaction with respect to $[\text{H}_2]$ |  |
| the order of reaction with respect to $[\text{NO}]$ |  |
| the overall order of the reaction |  |

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: Predict how the initial rate for reaction 3 changes when the concentration of $\text{NO}$ is halved.

parts.label: (a)(iii)
parts.text: Predict how the initial rate for reaction 3 changes when the concentrations of $\text{NO}$ and $\text{H}_2$ are both increased **three** times.

parts.label: (a)(iv)
parts.text: Suggest why reaction 3 is unlikely to proceed by a mechanism involving only a single step.

parts.label: (a)(v)
parts.text:
Suggest equations for the **three** steps of the reaction mechanism for reaction 3.

Each step involves a reaction between **two** molecules.

step 1 $$\ldots\ldots \rightarrow \ldots\ldots$$

step 2 $$\ldots\ldots + \ldots\ldots \rightarrow \text{N}_2\text{O} + \ldots\ldots$$

step 3 $$\text{N}_2\text{O} + \ldots\ldots \rightarrow \ldots\ldots + \ldots\ldots$$

parts.label: (a)(vi)
parts.text:
Suggest the role of $\text{N}_2\text{O}$ in this mechanism.

Explain your reasoning.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Iodine, $\text{I}_2$, reacts with thiosulfate ions, $\text{S}_2\text{O}_3^{2-}$, as shown in reaction 4.

reaction 4 $$2\text{S}_2\text{O}_3^{2-} + \text{I}_2 \rightarrow \text{S}_4\text{O}_6^{2-} + 2\text{I}^-$$

Reaction 4 is carried out in the presence of a large excess of $\text{I}_2$. Under these conditions, the reaction is first order with respect to $[\text{S}_2\text{O}_3^{2-}]$ and zero order with respect to $[\text{I}_2]$.

The half-life, $t_{\frac{1}{2}}$, for reaction 4 is 720 s under certain conditions.

Calculate the value of the rate constant, $k$, for reaction 4. Include the units of $k$.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.stem: The reaction between iodide ions, $\text{I}^-\text{(aq)}$, and peroxydisulfate ions, $\text{S}_2\text{O}_8^{2-}\text{(aq)}$, is catalysed by $\text{Co}^{3+}\text{(aq)}$. The mechanism is similar to the mechanism of this reaction when $\text{Fe}^{3+}\text{(aq)}$ is used as the catalyst.
parts.text:
State the type of catalysis that occurs in this reaction.

Explain your reasoning.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Write **two** equations to show how $\text{Co}^{3+}\text{(aq)}$ catalyses this reaction.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text: Suggest why this reaction is slow in the absence of $\text{Co}^{3+}\text{(aq)}$.
